messages.text: Monday, September 21 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies, a hint of autumn, and local learning opportunities
Today brings overcast skies with a cool autumn feel, as the season edges closer to the equinox. Local events offer chances to learn new skills or enjoy live performances.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 61°F and a low around 52°F, with a minimal chance of precipitation.
Sunrise is at 7:20 AM, sunset at 7:33 PM, with the moon appearing as a waxing gibbous, 72.0% illuminated.
Learn something new or enjoy the arts

For those interested in hands-on learning, the AADL Pittsfield offers a free Beginner Needle Felting workshop at 6:00 PM. Alternatively, experience live music with Glenn Jones, Liam Grant, and Nick Schillace at Trinosophes in Detroit at 7:30 PM.
Collin's birthday is today, September 21.
Local incidents and community well-being discussions

A 19-year-old has been charged following a crash in Oak Park on September 17 that killed an Uber driver and injured a passenger. Separately, an article offers 10 ways to combat loneliness in the Ann Arbor community.
Tomorrow and the days ahead
Tomorrow, consider the immersive culinary series at Flowers of Vietnam in Detroit, or the Ann Arbor Festival of Song at Kerrytown Concert House. The September Equinox arrives the day after tomorrow.
Space navigation and cosmic history

NASA's Starling satellites have demonstrated GPS-free autonomous navigation using onboard cameras. Meanwhile, Hubble telescope data has identified a major merger from the Milky Way’s infancy, suggesting an ancient collision with a dwarf galaxy.
The schedule for the next Starship launch is unset, with independent estimates listing no earlier than September 18, 2026.
A quiet day offers space for reflection and engagement.
Tuesday, September 22 · Canton, Michigan
Autumn Equinox Arrives Amidst Clear Skies and Local Buzz

The Autumn Equinox arrives today under overcast skies, with a cool high near 64°F. Local events range from author talks and cultural storytelling to discussions on endangered orchids and the future of cancer treatment.
Today will be overcast with a high near 64°F and a low around 48°F, with no chance of precipitation.
Sunrise is at 7:21 AM and sunset is at 7:31 PM, with the moon a waxing gibbous at 80.3% illumination.
Tuesday's Local and Nearby Offerings

For an engaging evening, consider the talk on the endangered Eastern Prairie Fringed Orchid at U-M Matthaei Botanical Gardens Auditorium at 7 PM. Alternatively, Ann Arbor's Kerrytown Concert House hosts a French love and loss song festival at 7:30 PM.
The Lightning Robotics Parent Informational Meeting is scheduled for today at 7:00 PM.
University of Michigan Advances Cancer Treatment Research

The University of Michigan has established a $10 million Histotripsy Center to advance non-invasive cancer treatments using soundwaves. This technique, already FDA-approved for liver tumors, uses targeted soundwaves to break apart tumors.
Wednesday and Beyond Offer Music and Crafts

Tomorrow, catch a free concert celebrating John Coltrane's Centennial at Campus Martius Park in Detroit at 6:30 PM. For a more hands-on activity, the Downtown Library in Ann Arbor offers a Riso Lab workshop at 5:00 PM.
NASA Satellites Achieve Autonomous Navigation Milestone

NASA's Starling satellites successfully demonstrated GPS-free autonomous navigation using onboard cameras and a catalog of space objects. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has also cleared its flight-readiness review, targeting a launch soon.
The next Starship launch attempt is estimated to be no earlier than September 18, 2026.
May the day bring a quiet curiosity and a sense of connection.
